sentences.text:
And 4 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Azmi Yousuf,Amit Kumar Awasthi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned Counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. None appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.
3. Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant today is taken on record.
4. This is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.
The first bail application was rejected vide order dated 14.3.2022 passed by another Co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that subsequent to the rejection of the first bail application, the fact witnesses have already deposed and the applicant still continues to languish in Hanif vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27211474/
1 jail since 28.9.2020 having no criminal history and the trial is proceeding at a tardy pace and there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in near future.

entities.text: Hanif vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, according to the applicant, prima facie his right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India of speedy trial is adversely affected as such looking to the period of incarceration of the applicant who has spent almost three and half years in jail, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has strongly opposed the prayer for bail.
He however does not dispute that the applicant is in jail since 28.9.2020.

7. Solely considering the period of pre trial detention of the applicant who is languishing in jail since 28.9.2020 and there being no likelihood of the trial being concluded in the near future, the right of the applicant enshrined by virtue of Article 21 of the Constitution of India are prima facie violated,
and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and more so when the facts witnesses have already been examined and without expressing any opinion on merit
, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, the present application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant Mr. Hanif be released on bail in Crime/ FIR No.0153 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(2) (v) of the SC & ST Act,
Police Station Tikonia, District Lakhimpur Kheri on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions: -
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 14.3.2024 Shukla  Hanif vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27211474/
